recipes.name: Strawberry Pizza
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (2 ounce) package strawberry Danish dessert mix (e.g. Junket)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix flour and confectioners' sugar together in a medium bowl. Stir in melted butter. Press mixture evenly into a 12-inch pizza pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Allow to cool.
While the crust is cooling, beat cream cheese and white sugar in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer until smooth.
Spread cream cheese mixture over cooled crust, then arrange strawberries over top.

Combine custard dessert mix and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil while stirring frequently. Boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour mixture over strawberry layer. Chill before serving, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Pizza
raw_recipe.description: This whimsical strawberry pizza features a sweet dough that's topped with sweetened cream cheese and sliced berries and finished with a tasty custard.

review.reviewBody: Made it for 4th of July and everyone liked it. I couldn't find the danish mix, instead I used the strawberry glazed.

I've made variations of this in the past and always felt they were a little too uniformly sweet. So with this one, I omitted the sugar from the crust and only put in 1/4 cup powdered sugar with the cream cheese. This helped bring out the individual flavors of the different layers - the strawberries and glaze give it enough sweetness! Also brings down the calorie count.

Also, for the glaze, I couldn't find Danish Dessert so I made my own glaze of 1 c. white sugar, 1 c. water and 2 tbs corn starch - bring to boil so it thickens, then remove from heat and add in 3 tbs. strawberry Jell-O. I didn't use all of it on the pizza either - just drizzled on as much as I wanted.

Changed settings to 24 servings. We used a un greased 13 x 9 glass dish. Baked at 350 for 22 minutes. We used Marie's strawberry glaze and the results were incredible. My family already put in requests for this dish at our next gathering.

After mixing the ing. for the crust it was not enough to cover a 12 inch pizza pan. I made it in a 8x12 pan. I couldn't believe 3 simple ingredients made such a delicious crust. Instead of the topping in the recipe, I melted chocolate chips and drizzled them on top of the strawberries. Nothing better than strawberries and chocolate!
So good! I did it in a 10” tart pan. Served with ice cream and salted caramel chocolate sauce drizzled over top!
I made it with strawberries i macerated in sugar as my topping and glaze
I made this using a sugar cookie base for the crust. Turned out great!
Made it in a 9x13 pan as I didn’t have a pizza pan. Worked fine. We had 5 out of 6 give it a thumbs up.
Made this in the summer. Now that Christmas is here, my family and friends are asking for it again. It's absolutely delicious!
I tried it with blueberries inside and strawberries on top. It tasted WOUNDERFUL.
The crust is super good and easy to make. I changed the toppings though, 8 oz cream cheese mixed with one jar of marshmallow cream. Then I added strawberries on top. Any fruit would work:)

This is my favorite dessert pizza recipe! The crust is delicious, light, flakey, chewy ... almost like a cookie. It holds the juices well and doesn' get soggy. The junket is awesome (much lighter than other glaze recipes and not as sweet). An amazing dessert .... especially for summer!

I have tried many versions of fruit pizza, this is by FAR my fave! The cookie is delicious, and its harder so it doesn't get soggy. The junket is a million times better than glaze, not so thick and gaggy. Everybody I've made this for loves it!
Was disappointed in this. The crust was too wet and runny. Unable to pat it down because of this. I believe it needs more flour.

I made this for a gathering and it was a hit. Cools you down after a hot and spicy dinner. I didn't have any junket so I used dessert pudding mix and cut down the milk by about half. Quick and easy for an "oh my gosh,I forgot about the potluck dinner" moment.
